lines.text: [warm] Your blog can fill itself. Here's how publishing works.
Ryze writes articles for you — but they need somewhere to live. That's your website. Connect it once — Shopify, WordPress, whatever runs your site — and Ryze gets a door to publish through.
That's the whole setup. You never touch this again.
Now, the plan. Ryze already researched what your customers search for, and turned it into articles. Every row targets a real query people type into Google — nothing here is invented.
[curious] Planned means it's just a topic so far. A keyword worth writing about, waiting its turn.

And you don't have to touch them. On its scheduled day, each planned topic writes itself and turns into a draft. If automatic publishing is on, it goes live that same day. If not — it simply waits in Drafted for your review.
Don't want to wait? [curious] Open any planned topic — and hit Generate now. Ryze starts writing it right away.
Drafted means the article is fully written — and waiting for you to look at it.
And published means it's live on your site. With real results right next to it — impressions, and the traffic trend for every article.
Let's look at a draft before it goes out.
You read it the way your customer will. And on the right — the score. Ryze checks the structure, the links, the keywords — so you don't need to know SEO to judge an article.
Want something changed without editing by hand? [curious] Ask the agent. It reads the article and rewrites exactly what you tell it to.
Or edit it yourself.
Everything here is yours to change — the address, the meta tags Google reads, the day it goes out.
Even the picture. One click — a new one.
Save, and step back to the article.
[excited] Happy with it? Publish. A few minutes later, it's live on your site.
And here's the real point — you don't have to publish by hand at all. In settings, switch publishing to automatic. From then on, every article goes live on its scheduled day, about five a day.
Moved your site? Change where articles go, right here — and new articles follow.
Already-published articles can move too. [curious] Republish — push it again, or send it to the new platform, and Ryze removes the old copy for you.
So — connect once, review the drafts you care about, and let the rest publish itself. [smiling] That's a blog that fills itself.
